responses.sql: SELECT SUM(rebtotal) AS total_rebate, AVG(feerate - rebrate) AS avg_net_fee_rate FROM fees WHERE rebrate > 0.0005

assumptions.assumption: 'High-rebate' means rebrate strictly greater than 0.0005 (cutoff excluded).
Average net fee rate is computed per record as feerate - rebrate, only over records where both values are non-null (AVG ignores nulls); SUM and AVG return NULL when no rows qualify.

alternatives.interpretation: High-rebate means rebrate at or above the cutoff (>= 0.0005).

assumptions.assumption: "High-rebate" means rebrate strictly greater than 0.0005 (cutoff excluded).

The average net fee rate is computed per row as feerate - rebrate and then averaged. Rows where either value is NULL are skipped by AVG, and rows with a NULL rebtotal are skipped by SUM. With no qualifying rows, both values come back NULL.

alternatives.interpretation: High-rebate means rebrate at or above 0.0005 (cutoff included).

assumptions.assumption: "High-rebate" means rebrate strictly greater than 0.0005 (the cutoff itself is excluded).
Rows where feerate or rebrate is NULL are ignored in the average (NULL arithmetic); rows with NULL rebtotal are ignored in the sum. With no qualifying rows, both values are NULL.
